title: Graph Valid Tree
keyIdea: A tree = connected + no cycle, which also forces exactly n − 1 edges. Check the count, then DFS from 0 (skipping the parent: a visited non-parent neighbour = cycle) and make sure every node was visited. Or Union-Find: any edge joining two nodes with the same root = cycle.

approaches.name: Union-Find
approaches.idea: edges == n − 1, then union every edge; equal roots → false; otherwise true.
approaches.why: n − 1 near-constant unions; n − 1 successful merges leave exactly one group.

approaches.name: Edge count + DFS with parent
approaches.idea: edges == n − 1; DFS from 0 skipping the parent; a visited non-parent neighbour → false; finally all nodes visited.
approaches.why: Each node and edge is visited once.

quiz.q: Why skip the parent in the DFS?
options: In an undirected graph the edge you came in on shows up again; it isn't a cycle
No: a cycle plus an isolated node can also have n − 1 edges

quiz.q: In the Union-Find version, why is no connectivity check needed at the end?
options: n − 1 successful merges take n groups down to exactly 1

quiz.q: What makes a graph a tree?
options: Connected and no cycles (and so n − 1 edges)
